newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends down on steady fund selling.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends down on steady fund selling.

text.p: NEW YORK, Feb 13 Reuter) - NYCE cotton futures closed lower on steady fund selling that attempted to push the spot March contract under support at 73.00 cents a pound and spark export business, traders said.
"The funds were selling all day long. They'd let up a for a few minutes and come again," a trader said.
Trade buying held the most-active contract over support.
USDA put new sales for the week ended Feb 7 at 178,800 bales for the current crop, withing market expectations.
USDA Wednesday raised its export target to 6.5 million bales for 1996/97, putting pressure on the market to maintain its steady pace of sales.

O.A. Cleveland, a cotton marketing specialist with Mississippi State University, said exports will reach 6.8 million bales by the end of the marketing year, and ending stocks could fall to 4.1 million bales from a current estimate of 4.45 million bales.
"High carryover will continue to weigh on the market," Cleveland said. He said stocks must fall to around 3.8 million bales in order to buoy old-crop cotton over 80.00 cents.
March cotton closed down 0.21 cent at 73.21 cents after trading from 73.80 to 72.90 cents. The back months ended 0.28 to 0.02 cent lower.
Volume was estimated at 22,000 lots compared to Wednesday's official tally of 12,611 lots.
